provenance.what: The port-side law of the operator catalogue: one operator's INPUT ids and OUTPUT ids are disjoint.
provenance.law: A wire endpoint has exactly one public name, "{nodeId}@{portId}". A graph synapse, a journalled edit and a pointer press all address a port by that string, so an operator that declares the same portId on both sides names TWO handles with ONE key — and a press on the output rect resolves to whichever handle the lookup reached first. `math.vector` declared `vector`, `x`, `y` and `z` on both sides; a press on its output `z` began a wire from its INPUT `z`, 40 world units across the node, and journalled the wrong endpoint.
provenance.rule: Inputs keep the plain noun. An output that would repeat one of its own operator's input ids is spelled with the `suffix` — `produced_channel_id` in the neural engine, which every auto-registered schema component and every hand-written colliding operator uses. Display names (code, abbreviation, fullName) are untouched: this is an identity, not a label. Where an INPUT was simply misnamed the input is corrected instead, and the fixture names each such correction.

wildcardWhy: `core.variable` declares the marker `*` on both sides. It is not a port id: the flow bridge and the flow host replace it with the variable's own name before a handle exists (`if port.name == "*"`), so no node ever carries a `*` handle. The marker is the ONE exemption and the law names it.

correctedInputs.why: The displacement a move applies is an offset, the name `brep.xform.translate` already gives it; the operator's product is the moved `point`/`vector`.
